## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\) is generated by either specified Schur interval; each family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The indexed-family graded Nakayama criterion identifies minimal homogeneous generating families with minimal spanning families of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), in the integral symmetric-function setting. [source-2@L1522-L1540|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: **Conditional \(a=1,b=2\) minimality.** Under the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and accepted globalization \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\), both Theorem 5.4 families are minimal.
## Strategy
Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) under the accepted graded presentation. Then
\[
A_+=\pi(\Lambda_+),\qquad \Lambda_+J_v=A_+J_v,
\]
since the \(\Lambda\)-action on \(J_v\subseteq A\) factors through \(\pi:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow A\).

For \(a=1,b=2\), source-backed generation gives the two generating families
\[
F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2)
\]
of \(J_v\), each of size \(3\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]

By the accepted conditional globalization,
\[
Q=J_v/A_+J_v
 =\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
The accepted low-degree relations give
\[
(\bar x_0,\bar y_1,\bar y_2)
=(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1).
\]
This diagonal matrix is unimodular, so both image families are \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of \(Q\).

The indexed-family graded Nakayama criterion applies because
\(\Lambda_+J_v=A_+J_v\): a homogeneous generating family is inclusion-minimal exactly when its images minimally span \(Q\). [source-2@L1522-L1540|claim=formal-document] Since both image families are bases, both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are inclusion-minimal generating families of \(J_v\).

Thus the requested **conditional \(a=1,b=2\) minimality result is established**.

## Gaps
The conclusion remains conditional on the accepted integral graded box/Schur/Pieri presentation and its exact basis statement for \(Q\). No unconditional or general-\((a,b)\) minimality assertion follows.
